_comment: Known Minecraft/mod errors for the Game Error Scan. Each has patterns (regular expressions searched in the game's logs), a plain-English title and explanation, and a fix. {1}, {2}... in the text are replaced by what the pattern's brackets captured (e.g. a mod's id). 'modGroup' says which capture is the mod to blame. Add new errors at the end - this list grows with every Nexus update.

errors.title: Minecraft ran out of memory
errors.explanation: The game used up all the memory (RAM) it was given and had to stop. This happens with big modpacks, high render distances or large worlds.

patterns: Could not reserve enough space for (?:the )?object heap
errors.title: Minecraft was given more memory than it can use
errors.explanation: The memory setting is higher than this PC (or its Java) can give. Lowering it lets the game start.

errors.title: A mod needs another mod that isn't installed
errors.explanation: The mod "{1}" needs "{3}" to work, but it isn't installed.
errors.fixLabel: Install the missing mod from Modrinth

errors.title: Two mods don't work together
errors.explanation: The mod "{1}" doesn't work together with another installed mod.

errors.title: A mod is made for a different Minecraft version
errors.explanation: The mod "{1}" was made for another version of Minecraft, so it can't load in this one.
errors.fixLabel: Update "{1}" (or switch it off if there's no update)

errors.title: The same mod is installed twice
errors.explanation: The mod "{1}" is in the mods folder more than once (probably two versions of it).

errors.title: A mod crashed while loading
errors.explanation: The mod "{1}" failed to load - usually it's outdated, or doesn't work with another mod.

errors.title: The shaders crashed the game
errors.explanation: The shader pack failed, often because the graphics card or its driver can't handle it.

patterns: WGL: The driver does not appear to support OpenGL
errors.title: The graphics driver had a problem
errors.explanation: Minecraft couldn't talk to the graphics card properly. Updating your graphics driver (from NVIDIA, AMD or Intel's website) usually fixes this.

patterns: has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime
errors.title: Something needs a newer Java
errors.explanation: A mod (or the game) was made for a newer Java than the one being used. This usually means a mod is for a different Minecraft version.
errors.fixLabel: Re-download the game and its Java

errors.title: Some game system files are missing
errors.explanation: Files the game needs to open its window and play sound are missing or damaged.

patterns: Error: Could not find or load main class
errors.title: Game files are damaged
errors.explanation: Some of Minecraft's files are damaged or incomplete (for example, after a download was interrupted).

errors.title: A mod's settings file is broken
errors.explanation: The settings file "{1}" is damaged, so the mod can't read it. Resetting it gives the mod fresh default settings.
